concepts.name: Line manager role and responsibilities
concepts.summary: Can state what a line manager is accountable for: team results, direct reports' performance, wellbeing and development, and day-to-day people decisions.

concepts.name: One-on-one meeting purpose
concepts.summary: Can explain why regular one-on-ones exist, whose meeting they are, and what they cover such as progress, obstacles, feedback and wellbeing.

concepts.name: Clear expectations
concepts.summary: Can explain why people need to know what is expected of them in outcomes, behaviours and standards, and how unclear expectations cause problems.

concepts.name: Basic goal setting
concepts.summary: Can describe what makes a goal specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound, and why goals link to team priorities.

concepts.name: Delegation versus task assignment
concepts.summary: Understands that delegation transfers responsibility for an outcome with authority to act, while the manager remains accountable.

concepts.name: Feedback types
concepts.summary: Can distinguish recognition of good work from corrective feedback and recall why both are needed and timely.

concepts.name: Onboarding stages
concepts.summary: Can list what a new hire needs: pre-start preparation, first-day logistics, introductions, role goals and early check-ins.

concepts.name: Manager's HR boundaries
concepts.summary: Understands that absence, discipline and grievances are governed by policy and law, and that a manager must know when to consult HR.

misconceptions.text: A manager's job is to be the best doer on the team and to do the hardest work personally.
One-on-ones are the manager's status-update meeting and can be cancelled when things are busy.
Good people don't need expectations spelled out because they will work it out themselves.

concepts.name: Running an effective one-on-one
concepts.summary: Can run a regular one-on-one with a shared agenda, listening more than talking, and recording and following up on actions.

concepts.name: Writing goals with measures
concepts.summary: Can draft goals for a direct report that state outcomes, success measures and deadlines and link to team objectives.

concepts.name: Giving behaviour-based feedback
concepts.summary: Can give specific feedback describing the situation, observable behaviour and impact, without judging character.

concepts.name: Matching tasks to people
concepts.summary: Can choose what to delegate and to whom based on skill, will, development value and risk, with a clear brief.

concepts.name: Structured onboarding plan
concepts.summary: Can build a plan for a new hire's first weeks with milestones, a buddy, training and scheduled check-ins.

concepts.name: Performance review cycle
concepts.summary: Understands the stages of a review cycle, from goal setting through evidence gathering to rating and discussion, and the manager's role in each.

concepts.name: Recording absence and return conversations
concepts.summary: Can follow the absence reporting procedure, hold a supportive return-to-work conversation and keep accurate confidential records.

concepts.name: Spotting early conflict signs
concepts.summary: Can recognise early signs of friction such as withdrawal, sniping or avoidance and understand why prompt, neutral action matters.

misconceptions.text: Feedback should be saved for the annual review so it can be given with all the evidence.
Delegate only boring or low-value tasks and keep the interesting ones.
Onboarding is finished after the first day or week.

concepts.name: Evidence-based performance assessment
concepts.summary: Can gather examples across the period, compare them against expectations, and write a balanced assessment that avoids rating biases.

concepts.name: Coaching conversation model
concepts.summary: Can use open questions in a structure such as goal, reality, options and way forward to help a report find their own solutions.

concepts.name: Career development planning
concepts.summary: Can hold a career conversation and agree a development plan with stretch assignments, learning and sponsors matched to aspirations and business needs.

concepts.name: Underperformance diagnosis
concepts.summary: Can analyse whether poor performance stems from unclear expectations, skill gaps, motivation, resources, health or personal circumstances before choosing a response.

concepts.name: Performance improvement plan
concepts.summary: Can set out specific shortfalls, support, measures, timescales and review points in a fair improvement plan, following policy.

concepts.name: Mediating team conflict
concepts.summary: Can analyse the interests behind a dispute and facilitate a conversation toward agreed behaviours, escalating when needed.

concepts.name: Managing long-term absence
concepts.summary: Can keep in contact, agree adjustments and a phased return, and work with HR and occupational health on prolonged absence.

concepts.name: Calibrating delegation level
concepts.summary: Can analyse a person's readiness and the task's risk to choose how much autonomy to give and how closely to follow up.

misconceptions.text: Coaching means telling people the answer more patiently.
Underperformance is nearly always a motivation or attitude problem.
A performance improvement plan is a formality to document a dismissal.

concepts.name: Tailoring management to individuals
concepts.summary: Can analyse each report's competence, confidence and motivation and adapt directive and supportive behaviours accordingly.

concepts.name: Calibrating ratings across teams
concepts.summary: Can evaluate ratings against peers' and defend them in calibration, detecting bias such as recency, halo and leniency.

concepts.name: Talent and succession development
concepts.summary: Can judge potential and readiness within the team and design development to build bench strength and reduce key-person risk.

concepts.name: Managing difficult cases legally
concepts.summary: Can assess a complex case such as repeated underperformance or misconduct, weigh evidence and fairness, and choose proportionate action with HR and legal input.

concepts.name: Team dynamics and psychological safety
concepts.summary: Can diagnose team norms, trust and voice issues and take actions that make it safe to raise problems and disagree.

concepts.name: Workload and wellbeing management
concepts.summary: Can evaluate individual and team workload, spot burnout risk and rebalance priorities or resourcing.

concepts.name: Managing remote and hybrid reports
concepts.summary: Can adapt communication, visibility, fairness and onboarding to distributed working while managing outcomes rather than presence.

concepts.name: Inclusive and fair people decisions
concepts.summary: Can evaluate allocation, development and discipline decisions for fairness and unequal impact across team members.

misconceptions.text: Treating everyone identically is what fairness means in management.
A strong team is one without disagreement.
Remote reports can be managed fairly by how visible and responsive they are.

concepts.name: Designing people management practices
concepts.summary: Can design rhythms, templates and norms for one-on-ones, goals, feedback and reviews that suit the team and organisation.

concepts.name: Evaluating performance systems
concepts.summary: Can critique goal frameworks, rating scales and review methods for validity, motivation effects and fairness, and recommend improvements.

concepts.name: Developing other managers
concepts.summary: Can create ways to coach new and experienced managers in people practices, such as case discussions and shadowing.

concepts.name: Managing through organisational change
concepts.summary: Can evaluate the people impact of reorganisation, role changes or redundancy and lead teams through it ethically and lawfully.

concepts.name: Building team capability strategically
concepts.summary: Can create a plan for hiring, onboarding, development and retention that closes future skill gaps.

concepts.name: Resolving entrenched dysfunction
concepts.summary: Can design an intervention for a team with chronic conflict, low trust or poor performance, combining individual and structural action.

concepts.name: Ethical judgement in people decisions
concepts.summary: Can evaluate dilemmas such as confidentiality versus duty, loyalty versus fairness or business need versus wellbeing and justify a decision.

misconceptions.text: A standard process applied identically across all teams yields consistent good management.
A manager can fix a dysfunctional team by replacing its most difficult person.
Being transparent about organisational change means sharing everything immediately.
